summary: Christopher Braider earned his PhD from Trinity College Dublin in 1982. He served as a lecturer (1983–1987) and associate professor (1990–1992) at Harvard University, and became a professor at the University of Colorado Boulder in 2003.

Christopher Byrne specializes in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD from McGill University (attested 2015) under doctoral supervisor Grace S. Fong, and also studied under G. Victor Sōgen Hori and Robin D. S. Yates.

Christopher D. Emms is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. By 2026, he was a PhD candidate in religious studies at McMaster University, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Shayne Clarke.

Christopher G. Framarin works in philosophy and Indology. He earned an MA from the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (2001) and a PhD from the University of New Mexico (2005), later holding faculty positions at the University of Calgary (attested 2014, 2026).
Christopher Hatchell works in Tibetology and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Virginia, where he was mentored by David Germano.

Christopher I. Beckwith is a scholar of Tibetology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at Ohio State and Indiana University Bloomington under Helmut Hoffmann and Thubten Jigme Norbu, he joined the Indiana University Bloomington faculty around 1976.

Christopher Isherwood (1904–1986) worked in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Corpus Christi College, King's College London, and under Swami Prabhavananda (~1939–1976), and held a post at California State University, Los Angeles (~1959–1962).

Christopher Ives is a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies. He served as assistant professor of religion at the University of Puget Sound (~1987–2001) and became professor and chair of religious studies at Stonehill College around 2001.

Christopher Jon Jensen works in religious studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his BA at the University of Saskatchewan and his PhD (2018) at McMaster University under James A. Benn, also studying at Kyoto University.

Christopher Kelley, a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who founded the Columbia Society for Comparative Philosophy, earned his PhD from Columbia University. He has taught at Columbia University, The New School, and Brooklyn College.

Christopher Key Chapple is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He served as a professor at the Institute for Advanced Studies of World Religions (attested 1982) and as Doshi Professor at Loyola Marymount University (attested 2001–2017).

Christopher L. Diamond is a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He earned degrees from SOAS and the University of Washington under Heidi R. M. Pauwels, and has held posts at Puget Sound, Wisconsin-Madison, and the Australian National University.

Indologist Christopher Minkowski studied at Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He served as professor at Cornell University (1989–2006) and as Boden Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Oxford and Balliol College (2005–2023).

Christopher Morris (1895–1980) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Tibetology. He taught at Keio University, the University of Tokyo, and the Tokyo University of Literature and Science, and was a controller for the BBC Third Programme (1943–1958).

Christopher Pinney is an Indology and visual culture scholar. He held a post at the Australian National University (~1987–1993) and became professor of anthropology and visual culture at University College London around 1993, with visiting appointments at Chicago and Northwestern.

Christopher R. Austin works in Indology and religious studies. He held a post at Concordia University (attested 1996–1999) and has served as an associate professor at Dalhousie University (attested 2022).

Christopher S. George, founder of the American Institute of Buddhist Studies, studied at Columbia under Royal W. Weiler, Geshe Wangyal, and Pema Gyaltsen. In 1982, he was attested as a professor at the Institute for Advanced Studies of World Religions.

Christopher S. Queen is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. From around 1989 to 2019, he served at Harvard University as Dean of Students for Continuing Education and as a lecturer on Buddhism, world religions, and the study of religion.

Christopher V. Jones specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He has held positions at the University of Oxford, the University of Cambridge (2019–2023), the University of Vienna (2023), and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Christopher Wallis works in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Rochester, Oxford under Alexis Sanderson, and UC Berkeley under Robert P. Goldman and Alexander von Rospatt, later teaching at Berkeley and Naropa University.
